Why
---
#12 and #13 (proposer z.wei, 'Reward contributor who donate z.wei to z dao')
each send 1 ETH to the proposer's own address 0xB073E9dfd5cC7313198920B5C85E80a8E2855646
with empty calldata. Together that is 2 ETH of a 2.438 ETH treasury. Each is
self-backed at 0.4533 ETH, 248% of the requirement, and becomes executable
2026-10-24 ~21:25 UTC. z.wei is still owned by 0xB073E9df..., and the DAO still
holds the same 10 names it held before (8 own mints + 2 transferred in by ross),
so the donation being rewarded has not happened, and it is claimed twice.
#11 (proposer 420.wei, same shape, 1 ETH to its own address) has zero backing
and is going nowhere, but closing it costs nothing in the same transaction.

Verified against live state: the batch simulates OK from the exec holder and
reverts Unauthorized() from any other address. WeiDAO is Multicallable and
Solady delegatecalls to self, so msg.sender stays the multisig.
